The map's label, in 1920 and 1930, for the Belgian Congo. The name Zaire is anachronistic: it was only adopted by Mobutu in 1971.

In these years the colony was being built up. Copper output from Katanga by Union Miniere soared in the 1920s, and the capital moved from Boma to Leopoldville, today's Kinshasa. Belgium also ran the former German lands of Ruanda-Urundi next door under a League of Nations mandate.

Labour for mines, railways and plantations was raised by force and by taxes. In 1921 the prophet Simon Kimbangu drew huge crowds with his healing preaching; the Belgians jailed him for life, but his church survived.
